description:
The BIOMASS programme was selected as the 7th Earth Explorer mission in
Spring 2013 at the User Consultation Meeting in Graz, Austria. The overall
objective of the mission is to reduce the uncertainty in the worldwide
spatial distribution and dynamics of forest biomass in order to improve
current assessments and future projections of the global carbon cycle.

The objective will be achieved by implementation of a P-band SAR mission,
providing global maps of forest biomass stocks, forest disturbance and
growth.

This notification of Intended Invitation To Tender concerns the procurement
of Biomass Biomass MGSE Batch#2 ? Test Adaptors by Airbus Defence and Space
Ltd as Prime contractor of the Biomass project. The supplier selection
will be made in accordance with the principles of ESA Best Practices.

The scope of this procurement covers the design, development, production,
testing and delivery of the Biomass MGSE Batch#2 ? Test Adaptors.

Adaptors are required to interface between the S/C and trolleys/stands and 
test facility interfaces. The side mating to the S/C shall reflect the 
launch vehicle adaptor design, while the other may vary depending on the 
intended use; e.g. vibration slip table for the vibration test adaptor. 
Where practical the same adaptor shall fit multiple interfaces to reduce 
the overall number of adaptors required.

In this framework, the present Invitation To Tender will be addressed to
economic operators (including those deemed to act as subcontractors) whose
registered office is established in such Member and Associated States
which, by the time of the Contract award decision, will be a participating
State in the ESA Biomass project.

description: Gegenstand dieser Beschaffung ist der Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung für 3 Jahre für die Beschaffung von neuen Insektenkästen mit standardisierten Systemschachteln (Unit-Trays) unterschiedlicher Größe für das Umbetten von Sammlungsmaterial aus stark biozid-belasteten historischen Insektenkästen an den Standorten Bonn und Hamburg, den laufenden Maßnahmen der Sammlungsmobilisirung für das Neubauprojekt neues Naturkundemuseum Hamburg, und die Aufbewahrung und die langfriste Konservierung der Entomologischen Sammlungen des LIB an den Standorten Museum der Natur Hamburg und Museum Koenig in Bonn. Für die langfristige Konservierung von Sammlungen des Kulturellen Erbes müssen die Insektenkästen in Bezug auf chemische und mechanische Stabilität bzw. Freisetzung von möglichen Volatilen Organischen Schadstoffen (Volatile Organic Compounds, VOCs) den Anforderungen von DIN EN 16893:2018 in den Anhängen B (Temperaturstabilität von Materialien zur Lagerung von Objekten des kulturellen Erbes), Anhang C (Stabilität von Materialien zur Lagerung von Objekten des kulturellen Erbes gegenüber Luftfeuchteschwankungen), und Anhang D (Vermeidung der Freisetzung interner Schadstoffe) genügen. Zudem müssen die Insektenkästen und Unit-Trays in Bezug auf Fertigung und Qualität die Anforderungen an DIN EN 16790:2016-12 (Integrierte Schädlingsbekämpfung, IPM) bestmöglich unterstützen und insbesondere Kasten und Deckel einen hermetisch dichten Abschluss und bestmöglichen Schutz gegenüber schädlichen Fraßinsekten bilden (z. B. Museumskäfer oder Motten). Die Insektenkästen müssen das Sammlungsgut sicher aufbewahren und seine einfache Handhabung sicherstellen. Bei der Herstellung ist besonderer Wert darauf zu legen, dass die einzelnen Komponenten wie Hölzer, Lacke, Beschichtungen, Silikone oder Kunststoffe keine reaktiven flüchtigen Verbindungen abgeben, wie zum Beispiel flüchtige organische Verbindungen, Lösungsmittel oder andere reaktive Verbindungen (VOCs), die das Sammlungsgut schädigen können.

title: VERIFICATION OF SMALL SATELLITE FITNESS FOR PURPOSE IN NEW APPLICATION DOMAINS - EXPRO+
description: Private investment has stimulated the development of several new small satellite systems within Europe over the last five years. These exploit the reduced technical risk associated with technologies coming from previous ESA and Member State funded developments and benefiting from parallel technology improvements (eg miniaturization, materials etc) so that standard commercial practices can be followed.However, in many cases the privately financed and operated satellites include technical characteristics that create the potential for exploitation in other user domains where there is less acceptance of EO or where technical effort would be required to develop and verify the required information products and services. This may be due to the fact that the sensors are in some way unique or that the the overall system offers unique performance capabilities. Addressing this asymmetric risk structure is routinely practiced within ESA programmes however and given the connections ESA has with a wide range of stakeholders and the experience in supporting diverse EO applications development, ESA is well placed to fund the required developments up to the point where fitness for purpose is demonstrated for a well defined and clearly engaged stakeholder community which can then be the basis for private sector funded follow-on developments and customer engagement. This Invitation to Tender addresses this gap in order to generate an acceptable risk pattern for private sector investors (and the satellite operators) to support the necessary operationalization and commercialization activities. The overall objectives to be achieved are:(i) Accelerate the update of data, information and services from European small satellite operators among customer segments that cannot be effectively addressed by such private sector entities alone(ii) Verify, together with key organizations within the target customer segments, that data, information and services from the small satellite operators address an agreed set of priority issues/gaps and the demonstrated operational performance and processes are consistent with customer segment working practices and are therefore considered to be fit for purposeThis will require the contractor to engage a clear set of customers with requirements that cannot be presently addressed but which could be addressed by modifications to or with a small satellite system currently in operationIdentify a clear set of developments associated with the small satellite system in order to address the requirements of the stakeholders being targeted on a timeframe that is of immediate interest to the target stakeholdersElaborate verification exercises that enable a sufficiently convincing demonstration and verificationthat the developments executed have resulted in the enhanced small satellite system being capable to provide the required information under actual operational conditions to a performance level that is considered acceptable and within working practices that are compliant with the stakeholders operational environment. This should include a clear definition as to what are these threshold performance levels as well as a credible prospect of follow-on commercial uptake if these agreed performance levels are sufficiently well achievedIdentify follow-on mechanisms that can credibly support a transition to full commercial uptake
